q: Markov partitions for Anosov diffeomorphisms enable symbolic coding. A Markov partition {R₁,…,Rₖ} of a basic set satisfies the Markov property:
opts: T(int(Rᵢ)) ∩ int(Rⱼ) ≠ ∅ implies T(W^u(Rᵢ)) ⊇ W^u(Rⱼ) and T(W^s(Rᵢ)) ⊆ W^s(Rⱼ)
T maps each Rᵢ onto a single Rⱼ
exp: Markov property: when T(Rᵢ)∩Rⱼ ≠ ∅, the unstable boundary of Rᵢ maps across Rⱼ (Markov in the u-direction) and the stable boundary maps inside (s-direction). This gives a well-defined symbolic dynamics via the transition matrix Aᵢⱼ = 1[T(Rᵢ)∩Rⱼ ≠ ∅].
